## What the unit delivers

1. **`ci_boundary.py` (G3a)** — the skill hook contract checked end to end: the skill's own `ci-boundary.sh --pr 202` in a throw-away repo with a stub `gh` first on PATH and `/usr/bin/python3` (3.9.6) as `python3` delegated to the hook and passed its exits through: green stack → exit 0 `ci: pass #202@… · stack: #201 pass`; a failed `web` run → exit 3 `blockedOn: CI fail on #202@… (web): failure — … (run 9100)`; `--pr 190` → exit 0 on the `chainTip` PR with `· requested #190 out of scope (B-15)`, and the stub's call log shows #190 and #185 were never read. `gh` is used read-only (`pr view`, `pr list`, `api …/check-runs`, `api …/annotations`, `run list`; the stub refuses anything else).
2. **`check_trailers.py` (OM-01)** — passes: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>` (model = slug, `(1M context)` dropped; bare `Claude` rejected), `Co-Authored-By: Devin … <…devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` as Round 10 recorded it 144 times (it names no model → passes with a warning asking for a `Harness:` line; read leniently from the final paragraph because Devin writes `Generated with [Devin](…)` directly above it), `Harness: <harness>/<model-id>/<tier>`; operator commits: `Harness: operator`, a GitHub web merge (≥ 2 parents, committer GitHub, signed), or a signature that verifies against the allowed-signers file **as committed at the base**. Exits 0/1/2/3/5. No author or committer address is written to its report.
3. **CI wiring** — as tabled above. P34.1 owns the `push` trigger (CF-01): a marked `TODO(P34.1, CF-01)` in the docs job names the push-side step (`check-build-memory.sh . --first-parent ${{ github.sha }}`) and the test it must rewrite.
4. **memory_guard "landed = present at base"** — a protected record counts as landed only if it exists at the judgement's base: `--range A..B` → A (`A...B` → the merge base); `--first-parent` → the parent; `--staged`/`--worktree` → merge-base of HEAD with the committed LEDGER's `pinnedBaseSha` (b051732c), else `buildBranchBase`, else HEAD. A record added after that base is judged as new (`N`): it may be edited or removed until merged; files present at the base stay frozen/append-only; the four control files keep their region rules. Tests: staged edit of a seed ADR passes; staged edit of an ADR present at the pinned base fails `frozen`; a seed readout may be removed, a landed one may not; no pinned base → HEAD fallback (edit fails); a range judges at its own base.
5. **BUILD_INDEX record-shape** — the 0 `record-shape` candidates SEED-02a reported came from `judge_index` judging added rows without ever counting them (and DEFERRALS/manifest likewise); the WIP added the counts (b051732c..HEAD now reports record-shape 361/361). This context also found and fixed a real gap: the seq-uniqueness set was reset at every table header, so a row in a later index table (SEED-09's late-marker table, the `## Round 11` table) could reuse a seq of the main index unnoticed. Index tables (a PR or landed column) now share one seq space; corrections tables (no PR/landed column) still may repeat a seq. Test `test_build_index_seq_is_unique_across_index_tables`. SEED-09's marker rows 190 and 195 are unique across the index (checked).
6. **Projection on the seed LEDGER** — `current_projection.py generate` on the live tree no longer reports any `ledger/*` inconsistency; its remaining INCOMPLETE items are 20 `adr/dangling-reference` (SEED-11's reserved ADR numbers 156/160/161/174–177) and 62 `coverage/missing-id` + 1 `coverage/count-mismatch` (T4/SEED-14's matrix rows) — other units' pending work.

## Agent interpretations (labelled; for the orchestrator to confirm or reverse)

1. "A valid OP-25 signature" = one that verifies against a committed allowed-signers file read at the base; until OP-25's key is committed, a signature alone does not identify the operator (the WIP's presence-only pass is reversed). The default path `docs/build/tools/record_policy/allowed_signers` is this unit's choice; P34.28 owns the file and may pass `--allowed-signers` instead.
2. A Devin co-author trailer that names no model passes with a warning (the unit prompt: "Devin's trailers as Round 10 recorded them"); OM-01's "naming `swe-2-high`" is enforced only as a warning until Devin Desktop's real trailer is seen at T6.
3. Exit 1 = usage for `ci_boundary.py` (the skill's shared contract); exit 2 = usage for `check_trailers.py` (as memory_guard).
4. `--staged`/`--worktree` treat every record added since `pinnedBaseSha` as editable. During Round 11 that window covers all unmerged `r11/` work; the boundary `--range <chainTip before>..<after>` and each PR's CI range judge earlier PRs' records as landed, so they stay protected where it matters.
5. `make docs-check` includes the three checkers; `check_backlog.py` (also in B4 G7 item 1) is not wired — plan App. A names `-memory/-spec/-matrix` only.
